response.sql: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS order_share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id), ranked AS (SELECT customer_id, order_count, order_share, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY order_share DESC) AS rnk FROM per_customer) SELECT customer_id, order_count, order_share FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY order_share DESC, customer_id;

assumptions.assumption: Only customers who appear in Orders are listed. The total is the count of all rows in Orders. Orders.customer_id is NOT NULL, so no customer has a missing share and the 'missing last' rule has no effect.

Share is computed as a floating-point division (the count is cast to REAL) to avoid integer truncation, and it is not rounded. Ties at 10th place are kept by using RANK() <= 10. Ties within the output are ordered by customer_id, which the request does not specify.
